cells.tense: Right now you're here, and what you've been feeling your way through has landed into something you can see whole.
cells.ask: Name one clear thing you've arrived at and say it to one person today, plainly, no buildup. It gives you back a shape you can stand beside instead of carrying alone.
cells.core:
Plenty of days you can sit with a question that has no answer yet, read the next step, and take it — no forcing, no waiting for the whole road to show. You've got that going right now, and something has settled enough for you to name it. There's a wholeness to how you're holding it, and it's yours to say.

What's worth doing with it is handing it over: not the whole road, just what you see about it now, said once, without making it a case. Put it out loud and it doesn't close on you. It keeps opening as you let it out, and what you know about it gets firmer, not thinner, with each person who hears it.

cells.tense: You're bracing for a resolution that hasn't arrived — already living past the part where you're standing.
cells.ask: Write one sentence about what's true right now — not where it's heading, where it is. On paper, then leave it there. It gives you a place to put your weight while the rest stays open.
cells.core:
There are mornings you can hold an open question and act from what you actually know, picking the next step without demanding the rest resolve. Right now you're running ahead of that, trying to feel the ending before it's here, and the part of you that can wait has gone quiet.

What works is picking from what's clear, not from what you fear is coming. Writing one true line about today's version is small, and it gives you something solid to stand on. Direction taken from here holds even when the rest is still moving, and you'll find your footing faster than you expect.

cells.tense: Something in you is still standing at a threshold you've already crossed, waiting where a door used to be.
cells.ask: Pick one question you've been circling and ask someone a plain yes or no about it today. Just the question — the answer is theirs. Asking it puts you back in the room you're in.
cells.core:
When this runs well, you can be with a question without needing the answer — curious, open, taking the next step anyway. That readiness is the whole thing: not knowing the way, but moving through it, meeting each moment without dragging the last one along.

Right now you're holding back at the start, as if the next part hadn't already begun. One small move brings you back — ask a single honest question and let whatever comes back land. That act alone re-lights the quiet part of you, and the charge travels into the step you take next.

cells.tense: Right now you're inside it — and you're talking about it as if it were something already finished.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to yourself or to someone, one sentence about what you feel is happening here — no rehearsal, just the words as they come. It hands what you sense back to you.
cells.core:
Most days you notice what you're feeling about a situation without needing to announce it, and it steers you — that quiet, accurate read of your own state, the one you act on without thinking about it. That read is running right now, shaping how this whole thing looks to you.

What's left is saying it. One true sentence about how this feels, first to yourself, maybe to someone who was there, moves the whole thing from something happening at you to something you're in. The read was yours already; putting it into words is what's left, and the words bring it into the open where you can use it.
